results.title: Nebius to increase prices for Nvidia GPU resources from October By Investing.com
highlights:
Editor Louis Juricic

Published Sep 17, 2026, 09:47 AM

© Reuters

Investing.com -- Nebius will raise prices for its on-demand GPU services starting Oct. 1, the company said in an emailed statement, according to Bloomberg News. 

The price increases will apply to Nvidia H100, H200, B200 and B300 GPU resources, according to the statement. The company will also raise rates for certain CPU and memory resources.

The new pricing structure takes effect at the beginning of next month.

results.title: Nebius Raises On-Demand GPU Prices Up to 21% From October 1: What an H100 Hour Now Costs | ServerCalc
results.author: ServerCalc Editorial
highlights:
Nebius lifted pay-as-you-go GPU rates up to 21% on October 1 — H100 to $4.50 an hour, B300 to $9.50 — the second rise since spring as AI capacity sells out.

October 12, 2026 ServerCalc Editorial 5 min read

...

## What changed

From October 1, 2026, Nebius raised its on-demand, pay-as-you-go rates across its four current Nvidia platforms. On its own published price list the per-GPU-hour numbers now read: H100 NVLink at $4.50, up from $3.85 (about 17%); H200 NVLink at $5.40, up from $4.50 (20%); B200 NVLink at $8.50, up from $7.15 (about 19%); and B300 NVLink at $9.50, up from $7.85 (21%). CPU-only servers were caught in the same round — the AMD EPYC Genoa vCPU now lists at $0.015 per CPU-hour, roughly a quarter more than before. Separately, from October 8 the provider moved preemptible capacity for these platforms onto dynamic spot pricing, so the cheap interruptible tier no longer has a fixed rate.

These are list prices for on-demand use. Committed and reserved terms are quoted separately and run well below the hourly rate; the increase lands hardest on buyers who pay by the hour with no commitment.

...

Figures in this piece are from Nebius's published compute pricing page and from reporting by The Motley Fool on the October 1 increase, cross-checked against the provider's own effective-date notice.

results.title: AI Cloud Firm Nebius Hikes GPU, CPU Prices | Silicon UK Tech
results.author: Matthew Broersma
highlights:
By Matthew Broersma, September 18, 2026, 9:00 am 

Amsterdam-based AI cloud provider Nebius said on Thursday it would raise prices for renting GPU and CPU capacity, in an indication of sustained demand for training and deploying AI models.

The move came after competitor CoreWeave said earlier in the day that it is signing new contracts at higher prices.

...

## Price hike

As of 1 October, Nebius said it would charge roughly 17 percent more for Nvidia H100 instances and 21 percent for the newer Nvidia B300, while rates for the AMD Epyc Genoa server CPU would rise by 25 percent.

Memory offerings are to rise by 41 percent, Nebius said.

The hike was Nebius’ second in three months, with pricing for B300 instances rising a cumulative 56 percent.

The company said customers reserving large-scale clusters for multiple months can receive discounts.

results.title: AWS Raised GPU Rental Prices Twice in 2026. Nebius Just Did It Again. — AIntOps
highlights:
AWS raised EC2 Capacity Block pricing for GPU instances roughly 15% in January 2026 and another 20% in July. Nebius raised its on-demand GPU prices again on October 1 — the second increase in three months, with some memory pricing up about 41%. Neither company frames these as one-time corrections. They read as a new baseline: the rental price of a GPU is no longer a number you can assume holds from one quarter to the next.

Published October 19, 2026 · 7 min read

## AWS: two hikes, one product line

AWS's EC2 Capacity Block pricing for ML instances moved twice this year. The first increase, reported to take effect around January 4-6, raised rates on the P5 family by roughly 15% — p5e.48xlarge went from $34.61 to $39.80 per hour, and p5en.48xlarge from $36.18 to $41.61. Asked about the change, an AWS spokesperson told Data Center Dynamics it reflects "the supply/demand patterns we expect this quarter." The second increase landed July 1, roughly 20%, across the P6-B300, P6-B200, P5, P5e, P5en, and P4de families — one report lists the P6-B300 now billing at $14.04 per accelerator-hour. Both changes applied specifically to Capacity Block reservations, not general on-demand EC2 pricing.

## Nebius: the same pattern, a shorter interval

Nebius notified customers on September 17 that on-demand AI cloud prices would rise again starting October 1 — its second increase in roughly three months. The headline move: H100 GPU-hour pricing went from $3.85 to $4.50, about 17%, with some memory pricing up roughly 41%. The company's own framing points to tight capacity, the same pressure AWS cited.

results.author: Finimize Newsroom
highlights:
The neocloud firm will lift pay-as-you-go rates 17%-21% from October 1st, as demand for AI computing keeps tightening supply.

...

What's going on here?

Nebius, a neocloud provider that rents Nvidia graphics processing units (GPUs) through its AI cloud, says it’ll raise pay-as-you-go prices for some chips on October 1st – its second hike in three months.

What does this mean?

“Neoclouds” sit between Big Tech clouds and companies that would rather not build their own data centers: they bundle scarce AI chips and the infrastructure to run them, then rent that capacity out. Nebius said rates for selected Nvidia GPUs will rise 17%-21%; it’s also lifting prices for some CPU-only, memory, AMD, and Intel offerings. highlights:
- 云基础设施提供商Nebius宣布将从10月1日起上调其按需GPU云服务价格，受此消息提振，其股价在盘前交易中大涨。此举被市场解读为人工智能算力需求持续强劲的信号，凸显了公司的定价能力和利润前景。
- 云基础设施提供商Nebius Group NV (NBIS) 宣布将再次上调其云服务价格，受此消息提振，其股价在盘前交易中飙升11.1%。市场将此举视为人工智能 (AI) 算力需求持续超越供给的直接证据，从而强化了对该公司定价能力和利润前景的乐观预期。
- 值得注意的是，这已是Nebius在短短几个月内进行的第二轮提价。经过连续上调后，B300 GPU实例的费率累计涨幅已达到约56%。这一系列举措凸显了议价能力正向云基础设施提供商倾斜的结构性转变，此前分析师已将此动态视为“新云”板块的关键长期利好因素。

## 价格上调细节

根据Nebius向客户发出的通知，新价格将于2026年10月1日起生效，涵盖了其主要的按需GPU云服务。此次价格上调的具体范围包括：

- H100实例：上涨约17%
- 最新的Nvidia B300 GPU实例：上涨约21%
- AMD EPYC Genoa CPU费率：上涨25%

值得注意的是，这已是Nebius在短短几个月内进行的第二轮提价。经过连续上调后，B300 GPU实例的费率累计涨幅已达到约56%。这一系列举措凸显了议价能力正向云基础设施提供商倾斜的结构性转变，此前分析师已将此动态视为“新云”板块的关键长期利好因素。
